content: 1. Do not administer ergometrine to women diagnosed with eclampsia, pre-eclampsia, or known hypertension. 2. Continue intravenous (IV) fluids containing 20 IU of oxytocin per liter at a rate of 30 drops per minute. 3. Perform continuous uterine massage until the uterus becomes firm. 4. If the placenta is incomplete or unavailable for inspection, manually remove placental fragments. 5. Administer appropriate intramuscular (IM) or intravenous (IV) antibiotics. 6. If unable to remove the placenta or fragments, urgently refer the woman to a hospital. 7. Examine for perineal and lower vaginal tears. 8. If a tear is present, assess its degree. 9. For third-degree tears (involving the rectum or anus), urgently refer the woman to a hospital. 10. For other tears, apply pressure with a sterile pad or gauze and position the legs together. 11. Reassess after 5 minutes; if bleeding persists, repair the tear. 12. If heavy bleeding continues, maintain IV fluids with 20 units of oxytocin at 30 drops per minute and insert a second IV line. 13. If IV oxytocin is unavailable or ineffective, administer 800 µg of misoprostol sublingually (4 tablets of 200 µg each). 14. Apply bimanual uterine or aortic compression if necessary. 15. Administer appropriate IM/IV antibiotics. 16. Urgently refer the woman to a hospital if bleeding remains uncontrolled. 17. For controlled bleeding, continue oxytocin infusion with 20 IU per liter of IV fluids at 20 drops per minute for at least one hour after bleeding stops. 18. Observe the woman closely every 30 minutes for 4 hours and keep her nearby for 24 hours. 19. If severe pallor is noted, refer the woman to a health center. 20. Assess the woman post-delivery by measuring blood pressure, temperature, and pregnancy status. 21. Protect the woman from falls and injuries, and seek assistance if needed. 22. Manage the airway if necessary. 23. After a convulsion ends, position the woman on her left side. 24. Insert an IV line and administer fluids slowly at 30 drops per minute. 25. Administer magnesium sulfate for seizure management. 26. If in early pregnancy, administer diazepam either intravenously or rectally. 27. If diastolic blood pressure exceeds 110 mmHg, administer antihypertensive medication. 28. If the temperature exceeds 38°C or there is a history of fever, provide treatment for dangerous fever. 29. Urgently refer the woman to a hospital if eclampsia is suspected. 30. For severe abdominal pain unrelated to normal labor, measure blood pressure and temperature, insert an IV line, and administer fluids. 31. If the temperature exceeds 38°C, administer the first dose of appropriate IM/IV antibiotics. 32. Urgently refer the woman to a hospital, as this may indicate a ruptured uterus, obstructed labor, abruptio placentae, puerperal or post-abortion sepsis, or ectopic pregnancy. 33. For dangerous fever (temperature >38°C) with symptoms such as rapid breathing, stiff neck, lethargy, or inability to stand, measure temperature, insert an IV line, and administer fluids slowly. 34. Administer the first dose of appropriate IM/IV antibiotics. 35. Provide artesunate IM (or artemether or quinine IM if artesunate is unavailable) and glucose, as this may indicate malaria, meningitis, pneumonia, or septicemia. 36. If birth is imminent (e.g., bulging perineum, visible fetal head), transfer the woman to the labor room and proceed with delivery management. 37. For vaginal bleeding during late pregnancy or postpartum, do not perform a vaginal examination. Instead, insert an IV line and administer fluids rapidly if heavy bleeding or shock is present. 38. If the placenta is not delivered, perform controlled cord traction to deliver it when the uterus is firm. 39. If unsuccessful and bleeding continues, manually remove the placenta and inspect it. 40. Administer appropriate IM/IV antibiotics. 41. If unable to remove the placenta, urgently refer the woman to a hospital while continuing IV fluids with 20 IU of oxytocin at 30 drops per minute during transfer. 42. If the placenta is delivered, inspect it for completeness. 43. Massage the uterus to expel any clots. 44. Do not administer ergometrine to women with eclampsia, pre-eclampsia, or known hypertension. 45. Continue IV fluids with 20 IU of oxytocin per liter at 30 drops per minute and maintain uterine massage until the uterus is firm. 46. For light bleeding, examine the woman and refer to clinical guidelines if pregnancy is unlikely. 47. For emergency signs such as airway obstruction, manage the airway, clear obstructions, and position the woman appropriately. 48. If the woman is unconscious, ensure the airway is open by tilting the head back, lifting the chin, and clearing any obstructions. 49. Insert an IV line using a 16-18 gauge needle, attach Ringer’s lactate or normal saline, and ensure the infusion is running well.
